newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FEYENOORD VS PSV - MATCH ANALYSIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FEYENOORD VS PSV - MATCH ANALYSIS.

text.p: Following is an analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of Feyenoord Rotterdam and PSV Eindhoven who meet in the Dutch first division at the Feyenoord Stadium on Sunday (Kickoff 1330 GMT):

Playing style: A 4-4-2 formation, with midfielders on either side pushing forward to support the attack. Feyenoord have a physically strong team who work hard, but lack some creativity. Libero Ronald Koeman commands the defence while Jean-Paul van Gastel takes care of the midfield.
Strengths: Strong defence led by the experienced Koeman and a reliable goalkeeper in Ed de Goey form the backbone of the Rotterdam side. The team is also renowed for its commitment.

Weaknesses: Feyenoord are still a developing side, with several young, inexperienced players on the bench. When hit by suspension or injury, uncertainty creeps into the team, leading to unforced errors.

Motivation: The chance to draw level with PSV in the league and the opportunity for their first title since 1993. A fanatical 50,000 crowd packed into the Feyenoord Stadium should fire up the players who will want to wipe out the memory of the 7-2 drubbing at PSV earlier in the season.

Line-up (from): Ed de Goey; Clemens Zwijnenberg, Geoffrey Claeys, George Boateng, Ronald Koeman, Bernard Schuiteman, Fernando Picun; Van Gastel, Kees van Wonderen, Giovanni van Bronkhort, Gaston Taument, Tomek Iwan; Pablo Sanchez, Henryk Larsson, Henk Vos.

Playing style: Former Dutch national coach Dick Advocaat favours a 4-4-2 line-up. In defence Jaap Stam is the linch-pin, with the experienced, but slowing Stan Valckx as a strong man marker. Full backs Vampeta, on the right, and skipper Arthur Numan, on the left, frequently push forward up the wings.

Strengths: PSV have a well balanced team with the creativity and fine distribution of central midfielder Wim Jonk and the striking power and deft touch of Dutch top scorer Luc Nilis. If the team is in form they are hard to stop. They have scored 66 goals in 23 matches, conceding only 17.
Weaknesses: PSV have an almost traditional dip in form after the winter break. They lost their opening league match this year against Vitesse and were knocked out of the Dutch Cup.
The attacking style of Vampeta and Numan sometimes offers space to the opposition.
Motivation: The chance to strengthen their bid for the title they last won in 1992. Their 7-2 home win over Feyenoord should add to their confidence.

Line-up (from): Ronald Waterreus; Vampeta, Jaap Stam, Stan Valckx, Arthur Numan; Wim Jonk, Marciano Vink, Ovidiu Stinga, Marc Degryse, Zeljko Petrovic; Marcelo; Philip Cocu, Boudewijn Zenden, Luc Nilis.
